A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP bouba-kiki study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical expressions, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResNet/ViT shape-word matching and Grad-CAM experiments in Figures 2–4, plus label-diversity and position-consistency analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds tokenisation examples, a label-selection case study, and results using alternative attention-scoring rules.

M1.justification: The CLIP architectures, probability-based label selection, and principal summed-attention Grad-CAM procedure remain unchanged. The expanded ViT description documents implementation details; entropy and centroid scoring are supplementary robustness comparisons.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 17 shape pairs, original pseudowords, English-adjective controls, and generated pseudoword families. The new appendix analyses examine retained inputs without adding languages, domains, populations, or task scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates entropy and centroid-of-attention rules against the original summed-attention rule. These add internal comparison methods; the evaluated CLIP variants, adjective controls, and prior human comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds supplementary testing procedures that infer shape preference using attention centroids or the image half with lower attention entropy, then aggregate correctness across images, labels, and prompts. The original sample sizes, ten prompts, and principal evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted checks of whether tokenisation preserves phonological structure (A.2), whether conclusions depend on attention aggregation (D.2), and which labels dominate for one example prompt (Table 3). Existing prompt, embedding, and position-consistency analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify Bayesian regression using four chains of 4,000 iterations with 2,000 warm-up iterations and report posterior means and credible intervals. The new checklist reiterates this practice without adding seeds, repeated-run information, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises label-diversity values, including ResNet initial words from .667 to .675 and ViT Alper labels from .466 to .450. New Tables 3 and 5 add results: sum/entropy/centroid correctness is .519/.488/.515 for ResNet and .522/.514/.515 for ViT. Main performance Figures 2–4 and the position-consistency values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs, and the regression formulas remain unchanged. The added attention-scoring comparisons introduce no formal derivation or new mathematical property.

C1.justification: The abstract and two stated contributions retain the same central claims: the tested CLIP variants lack consistent human-like bouba-kiki associations, and Grad-CAM provides a complementary evaluation aligned with human experiments. The additional analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism discussion changes substantially. v1 attributes difficulties partly to fragmented tokenisation; v2 argues that phonological structure is often preserved and instead implicates sentence-level contrastive learning and cosine alignment. It also newly argues that audio-visual models are unlikely to show substantially stronger effects and replaces the unresolved attention-metric limitation with robustness evidence.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an OSF code/data access link where v1 promised release upon publication, explains ViT CLS-to-patch attention processing and spatial reshaping, and identifies a MacBook Air M1 in the checklist. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the original experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Caron et al. (2021), Cuskley et al. (2017), Koriat and Levy (1977), Kouwenhoven et al. (2024), and Lake et al. (2017), supporting interpretability, orthographic, and cognitive arguments. The central positioning against earlier bouba-kiki findings remains.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits throughout, expands the Grad-CAM explanation and discussion, adds subsections A.2 and D.2 and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates title capitalisation, contact information, and venue text. The six-section main narrative and appendix organisation are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 5, redraws the t-SNE plots in Figures 5 and 9, compacts the Figure 8 montage, and relocates several displays. The original Table 3 becomes Table 4, and Figure 4's caption specifies ViT. Main performance plots retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v1 left alternative Grad-CAM metrics for future investigation and discussed tokenisation without examples. v2 adds direct scoring-sensitivity checks and tokenisation examples, alongside clearer implementation and access information, improving support and transparency. The gains are limited: the main experiments remain unchanged, and the stronger explanations involving training objectives and audio modalities are not directly tested.
